stem: A media company has 30 accounts in AWS Organizations. A compliance scanner that runs in the central security account must read resource configurations in every member account, and human auditors must sign in once with the corporate identity provider and get read-only access to all accounts. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: In each member account, create a read-only role whose trust policy names the scanner's role, and have the scanner call sts:AssumeRole
Register the security account as an AWS Organizations delegated administrator, since that alone lets it read resources in every member account
Attach an SCP to the organization root that grants the security account read access to resources in all member accounts
Connect IAM Identity Center to the corporate IdP and assign the auditors group a read-only permission set on all accounts
Create an organization trail in the management account and give the auditors direct read access to its S3 log bucket, instead of connecting IAM Identity Center to the corporate IdP

rationale: A read-only role in each member account that trusts the scanner's role lets the scanner call sts:AssumeRole and work with temporary credentials, which is the IAM pattern for cross-account delegation. IAM Identity Center connected to the corporate IdP gives auditors one sign-in, and assigning a permission set makes Identity Center create matching roles in each target account. Registering delegated administrator status authorizes a specific AWS service to operate across the organization's accounts using that service's own mechanism; it does not by itself grant the security account's role any IAM permission to read arbitrary resources in member accounts, so a general-purpose scanner would still need a role to assume in each account. An SCP never grants permissions; it only sets the maximum permissions available. An organization trail only centralizes API activity logs for every account; it does not authenticate people or grant them read access to account resources, and reading a log bucket is not the single sign-in with the corporate identity provider that the auditors need, so it fails that requirement even though the trail itself is a real, correctly described feature.
